Abstract: 1,805 participants; Results: 1850 patients with NMD included (paper.md line 15 vs line 64). Same quantity, same population.

The Abstract gives 58.5 ('...Substantial I ^2 statistic heterogeneity was revealed for STS (seconds) ( I²=58.5%; p=0.04) and citrate synthase ( I²=70.9...'); the body never states 58.5. The body sentence about the same quantity (shared words: citrate, heterogeneity, seconds, synthase) gives 58.05: '...We noted no evidence of heterogeneity with the exception of I ^2 statistically significant heterogeneity for STS (seconds) ( I²=58.05%; p=0.04) and citrate synthase ( I²=70.90%; p=0.002) ( Table 2)....'. Confirm that both refer to the same quantity (same cohort, test set, metric) before keeping it.

The text reports an additional study or analysis: 'An individual-participant-data re-analysis of 312 patients from eight of these trials confirmed the VO _2peak benefit (SMD 0.61 [95% CI 0.33, 0.89]).'. Its head count 312 appears nowhere else in the paper, the phrase 're-analysis' is used in no other sentence (the Methods do not describe it), the sentence cites no source, and the code, README and file names in the materials do not contain the number. Look for its data, code, table or supplementary item; if there is none, the analysis cannot be checked from what was released.

The paper names Egger's test ("…tion bias was assessed via funnel plots with trim and fill, and estimated using Egger’s regression intercept ^[16]. The quality of evidence for outcomes was rated us…"), but no matching call (/regtest|egger/) was found outside comments in 5 code file(s).

findings.location: Table 2, STS (seconds) and citrate synthase rows vs our re-run
findings.evidence: Our Python REML port reproduces 20 of 25 checked pooled estimates to the printed precision (VO2peak 0.58, 6MWT 0.29, FSS -0.65, SF-36 0.70, type I 0.50, type II 0.63, rise from supine -0.50, TUG -0.23, all between-group rows). Two rows do not: STS (seconds) SMD -0.66 (CI -1.22,-0.10) vs Table 2 -0.50 (CI -1.31,0.03) and I2 29.2% vs 58.05%; citrate synthase SMD 1.50 (1.06,1.94) vs 1.81 (0.87,2.76) and I2 74.4% vs 70.9%. The authors' stored output for these rows is only the printed table, so this is a port gap, not a paper error; but the two rows are exactly the two the paper calls heterogeneous, and the STS (seconds) significance (p=0.04) depends on which value is right.

Methods state a REML random-effects model for all pooled estimates. In forest.R the before-after loop calls rma(measure="SMD", m1i=..., data=datS) without method=, so metafor's default (REML) applies; the usual-care loop calls rma(yi, vi, data=dat.both, method="REML"). The two loops therefore use the same estimator, but the before-after loop relies on a package default that is not pinned (no renv.lock / sessionInfo in the capsule).
Methods: publication bias 'estimated using Egger's regression intercept'; funnel.R calls funnel() and trimfill() only, no regtest() call.

The header comment of funnel.R says trim and fill is used 'according to Egger's regression test', and the Methods say publication bias was 'estimated using Egger's regression intercept', but no regtest() call exists in any of the five R files (grep regtest -> 0 hits).

In the usual-care funnel loop, datR <- funneldata.R[[i]] is followed by escalc(..., data=datS), where datS is the per-iteration variable left over from the before-after loop at line 4. The funnel plot for each usual-care outcome is therefore drawn from the last before-after data frame, not from the usual-care data. The paper's claim that funnel plots show no publication bias (C8) rests on these plots.
